transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess the main thing is I just can’t sit still. Like, when I’m in the radiology suite or in class and I’m supposed to just be there, still, listening or waiting, it feels like I’m crawling out of my skin.

I keep trying to tough it out, because I know I’m supposed to be professional and all that, but I end up pacing or shifting around in my seat, or I’ll find some excuse to get up and move. Even stupid little excuses, like checking something or grabbing water. It’s been going on for months, and I thought I could just push through it, but it’s not really getting better.
Have you started or changed the dose of any new medications, such as an antipsychotic, antinausea drug, or antidepressant, in the months before this restlessness began?

Um… I don’t think so? I mean, I’m trying to think—like, I know what you mean, meds can mess with you sometimes. My roommate was on something once and he was pacing around all night, which freaked me out because I was like, okay, is that what’s happening to me?

But for me, I don’t really have a clear “oh, I started this and then it began” kind of thing. I’m not sure there was any new medication or dose change right before it started.

When you feel this need to move, are you also experiencing worried or anxious thoughts running through your mind at the same time, or is it mainly just a physical urge to move without much mental worry attached?

It’s more like… physical, I think. Like I’m not sitting there thinking through some huge worry spiral or anything. I’ll be in the radiology suite or in class and I’m supposed to just sit still, and my body is like, nope, get up, move, do something.

I mean, then I get kind of frustrated because I know I’m probably distracting people, and that makes me think about it more, but the first thing is really that crawling-out-of-my-skin feeling. I end up shifting around or pacing or making up a reason to get water or check something, even if I don’t really need to.
Did you notice this same kind of restlessness or difficulty sitting still back in childhood or your teenage years, or is this something that's only started in the past few months?

No, it’s definitely not just the past few months. I mean, it’s gotten more obvious now because the radiology training is so structured and you’re supposed to stand there or sit there and be professional, but my parents still bring up stuff from when I was little.

Like elementary school conferences—apparently teachers were always saying I was out of my seat, blurting things out, or rushing ahead before they’d even finished giving directions. My mom will joke about it like, “Yeah, you’ve never been good at waiting,” which is kind of funny but also… not really, because it’s still happening. So yeah, this was way before middle school, not something that only started recently.

latest_inference.note: Childhood-onset history (elementary school reports of being out of seat, blurting out, rushing ahead) confirms symptoms predate any medication exposure and have been present since early life, consistent with ADHD. No temporal link to antipsychotic or other dopamine-blocking medication was found, and the restlessness is purely motoric without associated anxious cognitions, making medication-induced akathisia (acute or tardive) unlikely. G25.71 and G25.81 are ruled out.
